rv.q: Judged as a family-friendly theatrical experience, it’s less satisfying.
This show is a piece of visually stunning but slowly evolving kinetic art, one that takes some patience and concentration to appreciate.
It’s a visually rich but ultimately disjointed experience.

cn.t: Robert Wilson's avant-garde adaptation delivers striking visuals and atmospheric tableaus but sacrifices narrative clarity, leaving audiences with a visually impressive yet dramatically confounding take on Kipling's classic.
